items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I used to carry notes to him from a girl named Annie Jones when I was 14

ctx.x: Everyone would give a certain amount of money for the food that was consumed that week and if someone came just for one day and night, they could eat as much as anyone else and not pay a dime.

I was given a weeks vacation without pay from the Western Union and it was just at the time the encampment was taking place. I had spoke about the encampment to William Smith, called Smittie by everyone, and a young man named Edgar Courance, who was a beginner on clarinet. He also lived on Carlisle Avenue, and I used to carry notes to him from a girl named Annie Jones when I was 14, and lived on Hathaway Street. Edgar was only one year older than I, but he was the kind of teenager that started liking girls when…

Edgar, myself and an amateur alto player named Alex Baker, used to rehearse at Edgar's house or Alex's house twice every week. I dont remember how I met Alex but I remember that he lived on Court Street. We could get orchestrations from a couple of music publishing stores up town and one we received was "Three O'clock In The Morning", which was a waltz. There was one place in this number where the trumpet part went as high as A above the staff and that was a note I could not reach, so I made a turn on the note…
